name: Black Hole in Thermal Equilibrium with Radiation
description: A static black hole in thermal equilibrium with a conformal scalar field, including its first order gravitational back reaction.
convention: In units $G=c=1$, the mass function is $m(r)=M(1+\epsilon\mu)$ and the redshift potential is $\rho-B$. The metric and its derived tensors are retained through first order in $\epsilon=\hbar/M^2$. The wall is at $R=r_{\rm B}$; the vacuum exterior has mass $m(R)$.
history: Radiation surrounds a black hole in thermal equilibrium, and its energy changes the surrounding geometry [york1993dressed, york1985equilibrium]. James W. York, Jr. calculated that gravitational effect in 1985 for a free, massless scalar field coupled conformally to curvature [hochberg1994potential, york1985equilibrium]. He found the change to first order in Planck's constant $\hbar$ [hochberg1994potential, york1985equilibrium].¶Don N. Page found an approximation for the stress of a conformal scalar field in the Hartle-Hawking state in 1982 [taylor2021backreaction, page1982thermal]. The state describes a black hole in equilibrium with thermal radiation [york1993dressed, page1982thermal]. K. W. Howard and P. Candelas calculated the stress in 1984, evaluating a remainder numerically and comparing the result with Page's expression [hochberg1994potential, howard1984stress].¶Static observers measure negative scalar field energy density near the horizon in Page's approximation [taylor2021backreaction, hochberg1994potential]. The radiation contribution to the mass is negative near the horizon and positive farther out [hochberg1994potential, hochberg1995canonical]. Its fractional contribution scales with $\hbar/(3840\pi M^2)$ in units $G=c=1$ [hochberg1994potential, hochberg1995canonical].¶A reflecting spherical wall encloses the hole and its radiation [hochberg1994potential, york1985equilibrium]. The interior joins a Schwarzschild exterior at the wall, with the mass outside accounting for the enclosed radiation [hochberg1994potential]. The scalar stress was calculated in infinite space, and a wall close to the horizon changes the field modes [york1993dressed, hochberg1994potential]. A characteristic scalar wavelength is about $42M$, and York considered walls farther away when using this stress [york1993dressed].¶York studied a cavity held at fixed wall temperature in 1986 [hochberg1995canonical, york1986canonical]. In the classical Schwarzschild problem, the locally stable branch has wall radius $2M<r_{\rm B}<3M$ in units $G=c=1$ [andre2021canonical, york1986canonical]. The two branches meet when the wall reaches the photon sphere at $r_{\rm B}=3M$ [andre2021canonical].

parameters.description: The renormalized black hole mass as a length, with horizon $r=2M$
The areal radius of the reflecting wall, $R=r_{\rm B}$
The value of $w$ at the wall
The dimensionless scalar field mass correction
The dimensionless scalar field redshift correction
The value of $\rho$ at the wall, $B=\rho(R)$

related.text: The vacuum geometry underlying the scalar field calculation, recovered as $\hbar$ tends to zero [hochberg1994potential].
A black hole in anti-de Sitter space, with thermal radiation confined by its gravitational potential and reflecting boundary conditions [taylor2021backreaction, hawking1983].
A black hole threaded by a cosmic string, whose thermal properties Erik A. Martinez and James W. York, Jr. studied with the Euclidean action [martinez1990].
